'''Killian Deron Antron Hayes''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|ɪ|l|i|ə|n}} {{respell|KIL|ee|ən}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 17, 2024}}</ref> born July 27, 2001) is a French-American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). The son of basketball player DeRon Hayes, he was born in [[Lakeland, Florida]] but grew up in France due to his father's professional career. From a young age, Hayes played with French club [[Cholet Basket|Cholet]] and excelled at the junior level: he debuted for Cholet's senior team at age 16 before receiving regular playing time in the following season. He was drafted 7th overall by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the [[2020 NBA draft]].

In 2019–20, he moved to Germany to play for Ulm. Hayes won the gold medal and earned [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors with [[France national under-17 basketball team|France]] at the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]]. He led his team to a silver medal at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2018 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]].

==Early life and career==
Hayes was born in [[Lakeland, Florida]] in the United States, in the same hospital as his father, DeRon Hayes, who was playing basketball in the [[American Basketball Association (2000–present)|American Basketball Association]] (ABA) at the time.<ref name="proux">{{cite web |last=Proux |first=Jérémy |title=Avec le fils, les Hayes font la paire |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/maine-et-loire/avec-le-fils-les-hayes-font-la-paire-4805139 |website=[[Ouest-France]] |access-date=14 January 2020 |language=fr |date=14 February 2017}}</ref> One year later, Hayes began living in [[Cholet]], France after his father continued his career in the [[LNB Pro A]], the country's top league. He played basketball from an early age, facing older opponents and often playing [[pick-up game]]s in Lakeland and [[Orlando, Florida]]. Hayes watched highlights of basketball games on [[YouTube]], drawing inspiration from basketball player [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[AND1 Live Tour|AND1 mixtapes]], to learn new [[basketball moves|moves]]. He grew up playing for [[Cholet Basket]], his father's former club, at the youth level. Although he wanted to play high school and [[college basketball]] in the United States, he remained in France upon the advice of his father, who had come from the American basketball system.<ref name=gardner/>

In 2016, Hayes turned down an opportunity to join [[INSEP]], a prestigious sports institute in [[Paris]], upon his parents' guidance. He began playing for Espoirs Cholet in LNB Espoirs, the French under-21 league, in the 2016–17 season and was five to seven years younger than many of his opponents.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |last2=Schmitz |first2=Mike |title=Jordan Brand Classic Global Showcase Scouting Reports |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/jordan-brand-classic-global-showcase-scouting-reports-5895/ |publisher=DraftExpress |access-date=26 March 2020 |date=18 April 2017 |archive-date=March 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326143610/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/jordan-brand-classic-global-showcase-scouting-reports-5895/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="sang">{{cite web |url=https://www.cholet-basket.com/news/killian-hayes-le-scoring-dans-le-sang |title=Killian Hayes, le scoring dans le sang |publisher=[[Cholet Basket]] |access-date=14 January 2020 |language=fr |date=16 February 2017}}</ref> In seven Espoirs games, Hayes averaged 4.7 [[Point (basketball)|points]] and 2.3 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] in 15.4 minutes per game.<ref name="lnb">{{cite web |title=Hayes Killian |url=https://www.lnb.fr/fr/proa/joueurs/killian-hayes-A72987.html |publisher=LNB.fr |access-date=26 March 2020}}</ref> In April 2017, he recorded 13 points, seven assists and five [[Steal (basketball)|steals]], sharing [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors with Addison Patterson, at the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cholet-basket.com/actualites/killian-hayes-co-mvp-du-jordan-brand-classic-global-2017|title=Killian Hayes co-MVP du Jordan Brand Classic Global 2017|work=Cholet Basket |language=fr |access-date=27 January 2018}}</ref> In the 2017–18 season, Hayes averaged 16.6 points, 3.9 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 7.2 assists per game for Espoirs Cholet.<ref name=sang/><ref name=lnb/> He was named league MVP after the regular season and helped his team win the Trophée du Futur (Trophy of the Future), being named MVP of the competition.<ref name="trophee">{{cite web |last=Durand |first=Jacques |title=Trophée du Futur : Cholet sacré, Killian Hayes MVP |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/lnb/430570/trophee-du-futur-cholet-sacre-killian-hayes-mvp/ |website=Basket Europe |access-date=26 March 2020 |language=fr |date=27 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=TDF : Killian Hayes MVP |url=http://tropheedufutur.fr/news/?id=1274 |publisher=LNB.fr |access-date=26 March 2020 |language=fr |date=27 May 2018 |archive-date=May 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502130119/http://tropheedufutur.fr/news/?id=1274 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Cholet (2017–2019)===
[[File:Killian Hayes.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Hayes with [[Cholet Basket|Cholet]] in 2018]]
Hayes made his debut with the [[Cholet Basket|Cholet]] senior team on October 21, 2017, at 16 years, two months and 24 days of age, playing two minutes in a loss to [[Nanterre 92]] in the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news |last= Rutard |first= Sacha |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/411774/killian-hayes-cholet-16-ans-est-entre-en-jeu-en-pro-a/|title=Killian Hayes (Cholet), 16 ans, est entré en jeu en Pro A|work=Basket Europe|access-date=27 January 2018|language=fr-FR}}</ref> In February 2018, he played in the [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp during [[2018 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Los Angeles]], where he was the second-youngest participant.<ref>{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Basketball Without Borders: Camp preview and full roster reveal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22360171 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=March 26, 2020 |date=February 8, 2018}}</ref> In his Pro A season finale on May 15, 2018, Hayes recorded 12 points and six assists in a win over [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]] for his best performance of the season.<ref name="guern">{{cite web |last=Guern |first=Thomas |title=Killian Hayes, le prodige de Cholet, "réfléchit à toutes les options" |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/basket/basket-killian-hayes-le-prodige-de-cholet-reflechit-toutes-les-options-5760594 |website=[[Ouest-France]] |access-date=2 January 2020 |language=fr |date=15 May 2018}}</ref> He finished the season averaging 2.2 points and 1.2 assists in 9.1 minutes per game, through nine appearances.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web |title=Killian Hayes Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Killian-Hayes/Summary/108654 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=July 26, 2018}}</ref>

Before the [[2018–19 Pro A season|2018–19 season]], he signed a three-year professional contract with Cholet after considering various other European clubs.<ref name="proux2">{{cite web |last=Proux |first=Jérémy |title=Killian Hayes, les coulisses d'une "négo" |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/cholet-49300/killian-hayes-les-coulisses-d-une-nego-5852074 |website=[[Ouest-France]] |access-date=January 2, 2019 |language=fr |date=June 28, 2018}}</ref> On September 22, 2018, after missing three weeks with back and toe injuries, Hayes scored 12 points in a loss to [[SIG Strasbourg|Strasbourg]] in his first appearance of the season.<ref name="rutard">{{cite web |last=Rutard |first=Sacha |title=Cholet: Après trois semaines d'absence, Killian Hayes revient ce soir contre Strasbourg |url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/440824/cholet-apres-trois-semaines-dabsence-killian-hayes-revient-ce-soir-contre-strasbourg/ |website=Basket Europe |access-date=2 January 2020 |language=fr |date=22 September 2018}}</ref> After his team was last place in its league early in the season, it parted ways with head coach Régis Boissié, who was replaced by [[Erman Kunter]]. Due to Cholet's struggles, Hayes initially believed he had "made a huge mistake by staying in Europe."<ref name=gardner/> At [[2019 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|2019 NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]] in February, he competed at the Basketball Without Borders camp for the second time.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Woo |first=Jeremy |title=The Best NBA Draft Prospects at 2019 Basketball Without Borders |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2019/02/18/basketball-without-borders-nba-draft-prospects-deni-avdija-khalifa-diop-all-star-weekend |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=March 26, 2020 |date=February 18, 2019}}</ref> On May 30, 2019, Hayes tallied a season-high 17 points, five rebounds and five steals in a loss to [[Élan Chalon]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mar 30, 2019 - Cholet 84 at Chalon-Sur-Saone 89 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-03-30/Cholet-Basket-at-Chalon-Sur-Saone/331635 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=2 January 2020 |date=30 March 2019}}</ref> In 34 games, Hayes averaged 7.1 points and 3.1 assists per game.<ref name="gardner">{{cite web |last=Gardner |first=David |title=Killian Hayes Is Coming to Claim His Basketball Birthright |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2847971-killian-hayes-is-coming-to-claim-his-basketball-birthright |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=3 January 2019 |date=2 August 2019}}</ref>

===Ulm (2019–2020)===
[[File:Killian Hayes Ulm.jpg|upright|thumb|Hayes with [[ratiopharm Ulm|Ulm]] in 2019]]
On August 2, 2019, Hayes signed a three-year contract with [[ratiopharm Ulm]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL), the top league in Germany, and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ulm gives the ball to teen guard Hayes |url=https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/9ud9sh38hc9uwe9j/ulm-gives-the-ball-to-teen-guard-hayes |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802183822/https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/9ud9sh38hc9uwe9j/ulm-gives-the-ball-to-teen-guard-hayes |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 2, 2019 |publisher=[[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] |access-date=2 August 2019 |date=2 August 2019}}</ref> He debuted on September 24, posting 15 points, six rebounds and six assists in a win over [[SC Rasta Vechta|Rasta Vechta]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Neuzugang Killian Hayes führt Ulm zum Sieg gegen Vechta |url=https://www.swr.de/sport/mehr-sport/basketball/ratiopharm-ulm/Basketball-Neuzugang-Killian-Hayes-fuehrt-Ulm-zum-Sieg-gegen-Vechta,ratiopharm-ulm-gegen-rasta-vechta-100.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191220170803/https://www.swr.de/sport/mehr-sport/basketball/ratiopharm-ulm/Basketball-Neuzugang-Killian-Hayes-fuehrt-Ulm-zum-Sieg-gegen-Vechta,ratiopharm-ulm-gegen-rasta-vechta-100.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Hayes played his first EuroCup game on October 2, finishing with eight points, nine assists and three steals in a loss to [[Virtus Bologna]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Virtus makes EuroCup return with win at Ulm |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/game-center/?seasoncode=U2019&gamecode=3 |publisher=[[EuroCup Basketball]] |access-date=December 20, 2019 |date=October 2, 2019}}</ref> On November 3, he recorded his first career [[double (basketball)|double-double]], with 11 points and 11 assists in a loss to [[Alba Berlin]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nov 3, 2019 - Ratiopharm Ulm 89, ALBA Berlin 109 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-11-03/Ratiopharm-Ulm-at-ALBA-Berlin/339252 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=20 December 2019 |date=3 November 2019}}</ref> Two weeks later, Hayes scored a then-career-high 24 points, along with five assists and three steals, in an 81–78 victory over [[Brose Bamberg]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Lupo |first=Nicola |title=Show di Killian Hayes contro il Bamberg: career-high da 24 punti |url=https://sportando.basketball/show-di-killian-hayes-contro-il-bamberg-career-high-da-24-punti/ |newspaper=Sportando |access-date=15 February 2020 |language=it |date=17 November 2019 |archive-date=February 15, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215214830/https://sportando.basketball/show-di-killian-hayes-contro-il-bamberg-career-high-da-24-punti/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On November 20, he tallied 12 points and 11 assists in a loss to [[Promitheas Patras B.C.|Promitheas Patras]], becoming the second-youngest player to ever register a double-double in the EuroCup, the youngest being [[Ricky Rubio]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Promitheas wins, eliminates Ulm |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/game-center/?seasoncode=U2019&gamecode=86 |publisher=[[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] |access-date=20 December 2019 |date=20 November 2019}}</ref> Hayes established a new career-high in scoring on December 18, with 25 points, five three-pointers and five assists in a 96–92 defeat to [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]].<ref name="brouet">{{cite web |last=Brouet |first=Christophe |title=Killian Hayes marque les esprits en vue de la draft avec une grosse performance en EuroCup |url=https://basket-infos.com/2019/12/19/killian-hayes-marque-les-esprits-en-vue-de-la-draft-avec-une-grosse-performance-en-eurocup/ |publisher=Basket-Infos |access-date=15 February 2020 |language=fr |date=19 December 2019}}</ref> He recorded 20 points and 10 assists in a 112–106 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] loss to Alba Berlin on February 11.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alba wins shootout, Gottingen triumphs over Bayern |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/bbl/1021240/alba-wins-shootout-gottingen-triumphs-over-bayern/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=February 15, 2020 |date=February 11, 2020}}</ref> When the BBL was suspended on March 8 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Hayes returned to his family in Lakeland. On 27 March, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref name="draft">{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=PG Killian Hayes entering NBA draft, 'excited' |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28962394 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=March 27, 2020 |date=March 27, 2020}}</ref> Hayes did not play in the [[2019–20 Basketball Bundesliga#End of season tournament|BBL Final Tournament]] held that June.<ref>{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Top NBA prospect Killian Hayes won't play in German league finale |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29151126 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=August 8, 2020 |date=May 8, 2020}}</ref> He finished the season averaging 11.6 points, 5.4 assists, 2.8 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game through 33 combined games in the EuroCup, BBL and [[BBL-Pokal]].<ref name=realgm/>

===Detroit Pistons (2020–2024)===
Hayes was drafted seventh overall in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Sankofa |first=Omari II |date=November 18, 2020 |title=Detroit Pistons select guard Killian Hayes seventh overall in 2020 NBA draft |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2020/11/18/killian-hayes-detroit-pistons-nba-draft/3767993001/ |access-date=November 26, 2020 |website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref> On December 1, 2020, Hayes signed his rookie scale contract with the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 1, 2020 |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Rookies Killian Hayes, Isaiah Stewart, Saddiq Bey and Saben Lee |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-rookies-killian-hayes-isaiah-stewart-saddiq-bey-and-saben-lee |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 4, 2021, in a 115–125 loss to the [[2020–21 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]], he suffered a hip injury, which was diagnosed as a labral tear two days later.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Report: Pistons Rookie Killian Hayes Diagnosed with Labral Tear in Hip Injury |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2925690-report-pistons-rookie-killian-hayes-diagnosed-with-labral-tear-in-hip-injury |access-date=April 2, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> On January 20, he was ruled out for at least two months due to the injury.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Killian Hayes' Hip Injury to Be Re-Evaluated by Pistons in 8 Weeks |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2927594-killian-hayes-hip-injury-to-be-re-evaluated-by-pistons-in-8-weeks |access-date=April 2, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> On April 29, Hayes recorded a season-high 11 assists in a 105–115 loss to the [[2020–21 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trister |first=Noah |date=April 29, 2021 |title=Hardaway scores 42, Mavericks beat Pistons 115-105 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000943 |access-date=April 2, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref> On May 9, he scored a season-high 21 points, alongside seven rebounds and eight assists, in a 96–108 loss to the [[2020–21 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hogg |first=Dave |date=May 9, 2021 |title=Vucevic's double-double, LaVine's 30 lead Bulls over Pistons |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022001023 |access-date=April 2, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref>

On February 11, 2022, Hayes recorded a career-high 12 assists, alongside eleven points, in a 119–141 blowout loss to the [[2021–22 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hogg |first=Dave |date=February 11, 2022 |title=Ball, Rozier lead Hornets to 141-119 win over Pistons |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100838 |access-date=April 2, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref> On April 1, he logged a career-high 26 points, along with eight assists, seven rebounds, and five steals, in a 110–101 win over the [[2021–22 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 2, 2022 |title=Hayes and Jackson muscle Pistons to 9-point win over Thunder |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401360976 |access-date=April 2, 2022 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

On December 28, 2022, Hayes was ejected from a game against the [[2022–23 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]]. While pursuing a loose ball, the Magic's [[Mo Wagner]] gave Hayes an arm-to-arm shove, sending Hayes into the Pistons' bench. This led to Hayes' teammate [[Hamidou Diallo]] pushing Wagner from behind and then Hayes punching Wagner in the back of the head, causing Wagner to appear to lose consciousness before laying in the arms of a player on the Pistons' bench for more than a dozen seconds. All three players were ejected from the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pistons vs. Magic altercation: Killian Hayes appears to knock out Moe Wagner with punch to back of head |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/pistons-vs-magic-altercation-killian-hayes-appears-to-knock-out-moe-wagner-with-punch-to-back-of-head |access-date=December 28, 2022 |website=CBS Sports |date=December 28, 2022}}</ref> The next day, the NBA announced that Hayes would be suspended for three games without pay as a result of the incident.<ref>{{cite web |title=NBA announces suspensions from Pistons-Magic game |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-pistons-magic-suspensions |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 31, 2022 |date=December 29, 2022}}</ref> He made 76 total appearances (including 56 starts) for Detroit during the regular season, averaging 10.3 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 6.2 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Killian Hayes 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683024/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=July 21, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Hayes made 42 appearances (including 31 starts) for Detroit during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], recording averages of 6.9 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 4.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Killian Hayes 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683024/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=July 21, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> On February 8, 2024, Hayes was waived by the Pistons.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has requested waivers on guards Killian Hayes and Joe Harris and forward Danuel House Jr.|number=1755718966348333261|user=Pistons_PR|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref>

===Brooklyn / Long Island Nets (2024–2025)===
On September 20, 2024, Hayes signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Killian Hayes and Tyrese Martin|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-killian-hayes-and-tyrese-martin|website=NBA.com|date=September 20, 2024|access-date=September 20, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on October 19.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Amari Bailey and Killian Hayes|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-waive-amari-bailey-and-killian-hayes|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}}</ref> On October 27, he joined the [[Long Island Nets]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Long Island Nets|title=Our official training camp roster 🔥 #StrongIsland 💪|number=1850674269581197342|user=LongIslandNets|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}}</ref> On February 19, 2025, Hayes signed a 10-day contract with Brooklyn after [[Bojan Bogdanović]] was waived.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Transactions |first=Ari Koslow in |title=Killian Hayes signs 10-day contract with Nets - Killian Hayes News |url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/498653/killian-hayes-signs-10-day-contract-with-nets.php?amp |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=FantasyPros |language=en-US}}</ref> In six appearances (five starts) for Brooklyn, Hayes averaged 9.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 5.2 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Killian Hayes 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683024/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=July 21, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He was not re-signed by the Nets to another 10-day contract<ref>{{cite web|last=Amico|first=Sam|title=Nets Opt Not To Re-Sign Former Lottery Pick Killian Hayes|url=https://hoopswire.com/nets-lottery-pick-killian-hayes-nba-rumors-news/|website=hoopswire.com|date=March 2, 2025|access-date=March 3, 2025}}</ref> and rejoined the Long Island Nets.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Grasso |first=Justin |date=2025-03-14 |title=Former Pistons First-Rounder Makes Next Move After Nets Stint |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pistons/news/former-pistons-first-rounder-makes-next-move-after-nets-stint-01jpba897z2d |access-date=2025-03-15 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

===Cleveland Charge (2025–2026)===
On September 24, 2025, Hayes signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. The Cavaliers waived him on October 16, but was then added to the training camp roster of Cleveland's [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Cleveland Charge]].<ref>{{cite news|title= Cleveland Charge 2025 Training Camp Roster |url= https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2025-training-camp-roster |access-date=November 7, 2025 |work=[[NBA G League]] |date=October 25, 2025}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2026)===
On February 23, 2026, Hayes signed a 10-day contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kings Sign Killian Hayes to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-killian-hayes-to-10-day-contract|access-date=February 23, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> On March 5, Sacramento signed Hayes to a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kings Sign Killian Hayes to Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-killian-hayes-to-second-10-day-contract|access-date=March 16, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> He made his first start for the Kings on March 11 against the [[2025–26 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]], recording 11 points and four assists on 5-of-9 shooting.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kings' Killian Hayes: Starting Wednesday|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-killian-hayes-starting-wednesday/|access-date=March 16, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref> On March 15, Hayes signed a two-year contract with Sacramento.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kings Sign Killian Hayes|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-killian-hayes|access-date=March 16, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> He finished the season having appeared in 23 games (including three starts), in which he averaged 5.5 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 3.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Killian Hayes 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4683024/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=July 21, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
While representing [[France national under-17 basketball team|France]], Hayes was named MVP of the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Podgorica]], Montenegro.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/news/frances-hayes-named-mvp-headlines-all-star-five1|title=France's Hayes named MVP, headlines All-Star Five|website=FIBA.basketball|date=August 20, 2017 |language=en|access-date=27 January 2018}}</ref> He averaged 16.6 points, seven rebounds and 5.1 assists per game and led his team to a gold medal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/Killian-Hayes|title=Killian HAYES at the FIBA U16 European Championship Division A 2017 - FIBA.basketball|website=FIBA.basketball|language=en|access-date=27 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/news/-crowned-u16-european-champions|title=France crowned U16 European champions|website=FIBA.basketball|date=August 19, 2017 |language=en|access-date=27 January 2018}}</ref> At the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] in Argentina, Hayes won a silver medal and was named to the All-Star Five after averaging 16.1 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.7 steals per game.<ref name=realgm/> In July 2019, the [[French Federation of Basketball]] imposed a six-game suspension on Hayes for not playing in the [[2019 FIBA U20 European Championship]] in [[Tel Aviv]], Israel.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ratiopharm Ulm signs possible lottery pick Killian Hayes |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/914772/ratiopharm-ulm-signs-possible-lottery-pick-killian-hayes/ |website=EuroHoops |access-date=30 January 2020 |date=2 August 2019}}</ref>

==Player profile==
[[File:Killian Hayes Brandyn Curry (cropped).jpg|thumb|Hayes (left), with Cholet, defending [[ESSM Le Portel|Le Portel]]'s [[Brandyn Curry]] in 2018]]
Hayes primarily functions as a [[point guard]].<ref name="magnotti">{{cite web |last=Magnotti |first=Trevor |title=Is Killian Hayes an NBA point guard? |url=https://fansided.com/2019/12/02/killian-hayes-nba-draft-2020-lead-ball-handler/ |publisher=FanSided |access-date=25 March 2020 |date=2 December 2019}}</ref> Listed at a height of {{height|m=1.96}}, he possesses above-average size for his position, although he is not regarded by analysts as an extraordinary athlete.<ref name="tjarks">{{cite web |last=Tjarks |first=Jonathan |title=Will NBA Teams Lean Overseas in the 2020 NBA Draft? |url=https://www.theringer.com/nba/2020/3/5/21166020/nba-draft-2020-european-prospects |website=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]] |access-date=25 March 2020 |date=5 March 2020}}</ref><ref name="berman">{{cite web |last=Berman |first=Marc |title=Hidden point-guard gem Killian Hayes may be answer for Knicks |url=https://nypost.com/2020/03/22/hidden-point-guard-gem-killian-hayes-may-be-answer-for-knicks/ |website=[[New York Post]] |access-date=25 March 2020 |date=22 March 2020}}</ref><ref name="ulm">{{cite web |title=Killian Hayes |url=https://ratiopharmulm.com/team/spieler/killian-hayes-45731/ |publisher=[[ratiopharm Ulm]] |access-date=25 March 2020 |language=de |archive-date=March 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200325230910/https://ratiopharmulm.com/team/spieler/killian-hayes-45731/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Hayes is [[left-handed]] and rarely handles the ball with his right hand, which sometimes limits him. He models his offensive game after that of [[James Harden]], another left-handed guard.<ref name="strauss">{{cite web |last=Strauss |first=Ethan |title=French prospect Killian Hayes could be special and is a Warriors name to watch in the 2020 draft |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1604862/2020/02/13/french-prospect-killian-hayes-could-be-special-and-is-a-warriors-name-to-watch-in-the-2020-draft/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=25 March 2020 |date=13 February 2020}}</ref> Hayes has drawn the most praise for his playmaking repertoire. In February 2020, ''[[The Athletic]]'' writer Sam Vecenie said that "his vision is absolutely off the charts, and his ability to complete passes off of a live dribble with his left hand is unbelievable out of ball screens."<ref name="vecenie">{{cite web |last=Vecenie |first=Sam |title=Vecenie's 2020 NBA Draft Big Board, 3.0: The internationals make their move |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1635879/2020/02/28/vecenies-2020-nba-draft-big-board-3-0-the-internationals-make-their-move/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=25 March 2020 |date=28 February 2020}}</ref> Hayes thrives as a [[pick and roll]] ball-handler and is comfortable operating in a half-court offense.<ref name=tjarks/> At the same time, he can be prone to [[Turnover (basketball)|turning the ball over]].<ref name=strauss/> Hayes displays good shooting form and often attempts [[basketball moves#Step-back jump shot|step-back jump shots]], but his [[Three-point field goal|three-point]] shooting is considered a work in progress.<ref name="cohen">{{cite web |last=Cohen |first=Zachary |title=Taking A Look At The 2020 NBA Draft's Five Best International Prospects |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacharycohen/2020/02/24/taking-a-look-at-the-2020-nba-drafts-five-best-international-prospects/#2786129b39bb |website=[[Forbes]] |access-date=25 March 2020 |date=24 February 2020}}</ref> He excels in shooting off the dribble as opposed to in catch-and-shoot situations.<ref name=tjarks/> Hayes is an accurate [[free throw]] shooter and has good touch around the basket, with an advanced [[Basketball moves#Tear drop|floater]].<ref name=magnotti/><ref name=cohen/> He can guard [[shooting guard]]s and smaller-sized [[small forward]]s. While his lack of lateral quickness prevents him from being a great perimeter defender, he is more effective as an off-ball and pick and roll defender.<ref name="milner">{{cite web |last1=Milner |first1=Zach |last2=Pearlman |first2=Spencer |title=Killian Hayes Scouting Report (Collaboration) |url=https://www.thestepien.com/2020/02/14/killian-hayes-scouting-report-collaboration/ |publisher=The Stepien |access-date=15 February 2020 |date=14 February 2020 |archive-date=February 15, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215214832/https://www.thestepien.com/2020/02/14/killian-hayes-scouting-report-collaboration/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hayes has an American father, {{ill|DeRon Hayes|fr}}, who played [[college basketball]] as a [[forward (basketball)|forward]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State Nittany Lions]] in the early 1990s and left as one of the program's most prolific scorers.<ref name=gardner/><ref>{{cite web |title=Postgame Notes: Penn State 63, Minnesota 58 |url=https://gopsusports.com/news/2015/1/28/Postgame_Notes_Penn_State_63_Minnesota_58.aspx |publisher=Penn State University Athletics |access-date=25 March 2020 |date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=March 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200325230910/https://gopsusports.com/news/2015/1/28/Postgame_Notes_Penn_State_63_Minnesota_58.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref> DeRon played professionally in France, Portugal, Sweden, Ukraine and Russia.<ref name=sang/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/mayenne/killian-hayes-nba-et-jo-2024-dans-le-viseur-5211735|title=Killian Hayes, NBA et JO 2024 dans le viseur|work=[[Ouest-France]]|access-date=27 January 2018|language=fr-FR}}</ref> He spent much of the prime years of his career with French clubs Cholet and [[SLUC Nancy Basket|SLUC Nancy]].<ref>{{cite web |title=DeRon Hayes : retour attendu, pas encore payant |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/deron-hayes-retour-attendu-pas-encore-payant-1749458 |website=[[Ouest-France]] |access-date=26 March 2020 |language=fr |date=26 November 2013}}</ref> Hayes' mother, Sandrine (née Demiannay), is a native of [[Cholet]], France and is a former basketball player as well.<ref name="cholet">{{cite web |title=Killian Hayes |url=https://www.cholet-basket.com/personne/killian-hayes |publisher=[[Cholet Basket]] |access-date=26 March 2020 |language=fr}}</ref> His parents met because his mother's sister was the girlfriend of his father's teammate.<ref name=gardner/>
